item.title: Australia news live: Albanese defends social media crackdown against White House criticism; Qantas confirms direct Sydney-NY flights
item.description:
On Friday, President Donald Trump said he was "proud to announce" that, "effective immediately," he was "banning" CNN, MS NOW (formerly MSNBC), and Politico "from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' [of] FAKE NEWS!" News organizations "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America," he explained. "Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow." That move predictably provoked a federal lawsuit by the targeted outlets, which argue that it violates due process and freedom of the press. item.title: US judge blocks deportation of DoorDash driver shot by ICE
item.description:
A federal judge has temporarily blocked tactics used by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to conduct warrantless immigration raids on construction sites in southern Alabama in response to a lawsuit filed by a Latino construction worker who has been detained three times, despite being a U.S. citizen. U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Beaverstock issued a temporary stay Monday against several DHS policies being challenged by Leo Garcia Venegas, the lead plaintiff in a class action lawsuit filed last October by the Institute for Justice, a public interest law firm. The suit seeks to stop "dragnet raids" that it alleges target Latino construction workers without reasonable suspicion and continue detaining them even after they offer evidence of citizenship, violating the Fourth Amendment. Venegas, an Alabama construction worker and U.S. citizen, has been detained and handcuffed three times…

item.title: Harris joins El-Sayed on campaign trail as Democrats focus on Michigan Senate race
item.description:
The father of 9/11 hero Todd Beamer is lending his voice to a new political ad targeting Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed over his ties to anti-American streamer Hasan Piker. David Beamer, whose son was among the passengers who fought back against the hijackers aboard United Flight 93 on Sept. 11, 2001, narrates the ad backing Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers. The ad focuses on Piker’s past comments about America and El-Sayed’s decision to campaign alongside the streamer earlier this year. As highlighted in the ad, Piker said in a 2019 stream that America “deserved 9/11,” and said just days ago that the U.S. is worse than the terrorist group al-Qaeda. “Pound for pound as far as the number of deaths, yes, we have caused tremendous terror all around the world,” he told Axios. Piker has also made other highly controversial statements that didn’t make the ad,…

item.title: EU drops sanctions for Russian oligarchs Usmanov and Fridman
item.description:
Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman delisted in what Ireland’s EU presidency calls ‘a difficult compromise’ for the bloc The EU has agreed to remove two Russian billionaires, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, from its sanctions list, while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 individuals and companies accused of supporting the war on Ukraine for the next three years. With an end-of-Tuesday deadline looming to preserve the Russia blacklist, the EU’s 27 member states found a compromise that meant delisting the two oligarchs in spite of very few countries wanting this outcome. EU sanctions have to be approved unanimously. Continue reading...
